results.title: [PDF] Climate change, risks and ECB strategy
results.content: RESEARCH Risk Management (2026) 28:2 https://doi.org/10.1057/s41283-025-00187-3 Abstract In light of the European Central Bank’s (ECB) growing commitment to addressing climate change, this paper analyses how the ECB climate-related announcements affect banks’ stock market performance. The RAR are estimated for three different timespans: Pre-Event (four days before the announcement event), the announcement day and the Post-Event (four days after the announcement event) 2 Page 14 of 38 Climate change, risks and ECB strategy: what is the effect on European… significant movement in the days before and after suggests a certain anticipation by the banking market, probably linked to the growing attention on climate issues. Statistically significant abnormal returns around the announcement date highlight the ECB’s credible and assertive commitment to climate-related supervision and the different response from European banks rather than banks in the Eurozone or SIs. The sign and magnitude of the RARs Second, to understand the nature of these reactions is crucial to define the sign and the magnitude of banks reaction to ECB climate-related stress test.

results.title: Climate change impact on European banks - Banco Santander
results.content: The European Central Bank (ECB) released its “economy-wide climate stress test”, developed to assess the resilience of non-financial corporates and euro area banks to climate risks (transition risk and physical risk), under a range of assumptions in terms of future climate policies. The results show how climate change represents a major source of systemic risk, and how for corporates and banks most exposed to climate risks, the impact is potentially very significant. The physical risk impact is also higher than in the orderly transition scenario.
